units.t: Who I Am: Ser and Estar

learn: Spanish has two verbs for to be. Ser is for who or what someone is: name, job, where they are from, what they are like.
Yo soy, tú eres, él or ella es, nosotros somos, ellos son.
Soy estudiante. Ella es de Chile. Somos amigos.
lessons.try: Write four sentences about your family using soy, es, somos and son.

learn: Estar is for how someone feels and where something is right now.
Yo estoy, tú estás, él or ella está, nosotros estamos, ellos están.
Estoy cansado. El libro está en la mesa. Estamos en la escuela.
lessons.try: Say how you feel and where you are at three times today using estoy.

learn: A helpful rhyme: how you feel and where you are, that is when you use estar.
Soy feliz describes a happy person in general. Estoy feliz means happy right now.
Practice by sorting sentences into ser and estar.
lessons.try: Make ten sentence cards and sort them into ser and estar piles.

check: Soy de Arizona uses ser for...
Es enfermera uses ser for a...
lessons.try: Write three ser sentences: origin, job, trait.

learn: Ella está contenta (she's happy right now).
Estar is for states that change.
check: Estoy cansado uses estar for a...
Ella está contenta means she is...
lessons.try: Write three estar feeling sentences.

learn: El libro está en la mesa.
lessons.try: Describe where five things are.
Fill in a ser chart.
Fill in an estar chart.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Ser and Estar
lessons.try: Ser or estar sorting game.

learn: Seiscientos, setecientos, ochocientos, novecientos and mil (1,000).
Quinientos, setecientos and novecientos are special spellings to remember.
lessons.try: Write five three-digit numbers and read them aloud in Spanish.

learn: Ciento is used for 101 to 199: ciento veinte is 120.
Spanish does not use y between hundreds and tens, only between tens and ones.
lessons.try: Read the population of your town or a big number from a newspaper in Spanish.

learn: ¿Cuánto cuesta la bicicleta? Cuesta ciento cincuenta dólares.
Centavos are cents. Un dólar con cincuenta centavos is $1.50.
Comparing prices: más caro (more expensive), más barato (cheaper).
lessons.try: Look at a store ad and read five prices in Spanish.
Write hundreds words from 100 to 900.
Say five years in Spanish.

learn: Una bicicleta cuesta tres mil pesos.
lessons.try: Compare prices in a pretend catalogue.

learn: Mayor que (greater than), menor que (less than).
lessons.try: Compare number pairs aloud.

learn: Mexico has more than 120 million people.
lessons.try: Rank three countries by population.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Big Numbers
lessons.try: Big number quiz.

learn: Me despierto (I wake up), me levanto (I get up), me ducho (I shower), me visto (I get dressed).
Desayuno (I eat breakfast) and me cepillo los dientes.
Verbs with me are about doing something to yourself.
lessons.try: Act out your morning in order while saying each verb.

learn: Hago la tarea means I do homework. Juego con mis amigos means I play with my friends.
Ayudo en casa means I help at home. Practico el piano means I practice piano.
Por la tarde means in the afternoon.
lessons.try: Write what you do after school on each weekday.

learn: Primero (first), luego (then), después (after), más tarde (later), finalmente (finally).
Sequence words make your story easy to follow.
Primero me levanto, luego me visto, después desayuno.
lessons.try: Write your day as a paragraph using five sequence words.

learn: Me levanto (I get up), me ducho (I shower).
lessons.try: Act out your morning with reflexive verbs.

learn: Me acuesto: I go to bed.
check: Me lavo los dientes means I brush my...
lessons.try: Write your bedtime routine.

check: Me levanto a las siete means I get up at...
lessons.try: Make a timed routine chart.

learn: Se is for he, she or they.
check: Se levanta means he or she...
lessons.try: Interview a family member about their routine.

learn: Los fines de semana me levanto tarde.
lessons.try: Compare your weekday and weekend.
Comic strip of your day.

learn: Hace buen tiempo (nice weather), hace mal tiempo (bad weather), hace fresco (it is cool).
La temperatura es de noventa grados means the temperature is 90 degrees.
Most Spanish-speaking countries measure temperature in Celsius.
lessons.try: Give a weather report in Spanish like a TV weather person.

learn: South of the equator, the seasons are opposite. When it is winter in Arizona, it is summer in Argentina and Chile.
Navidad (Christmas) in Argentina is in el verano.
El ecuador is the equator. Ecuador is also the name of a country on it.
check: Which country is named after the equator?
South of the equator, seasons are...
lessons.try: Find Argentina and Chile on a globe and the equator line.

learn: En el invierno esquío (I ski). En el verano voy a la playa (I go to the beach).
En el otoño las hojas caen (the leaves fall). En la primavera las flores crecen (flowers grow).
Use the season, then what happens.
lessons.try: Make a four-season booklet with one sentence per season.
Convert three temperatures roughly.
Make a safety poster for one event.
Colour a climate map.

learn: Mañana va a llover (it's going to rain).
Ir + a + infinitive is the near future.
check: Va a llover means it's going to...
The near future uses ir + a +...
Mañana va a hacer sol means tomorrow it will be...
lessons.try: Present a weather forecast.

learn: Write a short poem about la lluvia.
lessons.try: Write a four-line weather poem.
Weather news broadcast.

learn: El bosque (forest), la selva tropical (rainforest), el océano, el desierto, las montañas.
Los animales viven en hábitats. Animals live in habitats.
A habitat gives food, water and shelter.
lessons.try: Draw a habitat and label its plants and animals in Spanish.

learn: El jaguar lives in the rainforest. La llama and la alpaca live in the Andes mountains.
El quetzal is a bright green bird of Guatemala. El perezoso (sloth) hangs in trees.
Las tortugas marinas (sea turtles) lay eggs on beaches.
lessons.try: Pick one animal and write three facts about it in Spanish.

learn: Tiene (it has): tiene cuatro patas (four legs), tiene alas (wings), tiene plumas (feathers).
Es (it is): es grande, es feroz (fierce), es rápido.
Come means eats. El jaguar come carne. The jaguar eats meat.
lessons.try: Play twenty questions about an animal in Spanish.
Draw rainforest layers and place animals.

learn: En peligro de extinción means endangered.
The vaquita lives only in the Gulf of California.
check: The vaquita lives in the Gulf of...
lessons.try: Make a poster to protect one animal.
Label an animal's body parts.
Sort animals by what they eat.

learn: El guepardo es más rápido que el león.
lessons.try: Write five animal comparisons.
Habitat diorama presentation.

learn: El comedor (dining room), el garaje, el patio, las escaleras (stairs), el techo (roof).
El refrigerador, la estufa (stove), el lavabo (sink), el armario (closet).
Mi casa tiene dos dormitorios. My house has two bedrooms.
lessons.try: Describe your home in five sentences.

learn: Barro el piso (I sweep the floor). Lavo los platos (I wash the dishes). Hago la cama (I make the bed).
Saco la basura means I take out the trash. Doy de comer al perro means I feed the dog.
Tengo que means I have to. Tengo que lavar los platos.
lessons.try: Make a chore chart in Spanish for your family.

learn: Siempre (always), a veces (sometimes), nunca (never), todos los días (every day).
A veces lavo los platos. Nunca saco la basura.
Una vez a la semana means once a week.
check: Una vez a la semana means...
lessons.try: Tell how often you do five chores.
Label a kitchen picture.

learn: Tener que + infinitive means have to.
check: Tienes que barrer means you have to...
Tener que is followed by an...
lessons.try: List three things you have to do this week.
Role-play asking for help with a chore.
Plan how to spend and save a pretend allowance.

learn: Many homes in Spain are apartamentos.
check: A patio is an open ___ space.
lessons.try: Compare your home with a Mexican home with a patio.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Home and Chores
lessons.try: Chore chart presentation.

learn: La tienda de ropa is the clothing store. ¿Qué talla? asks what size.
Pequeña, mediana, grande are small, medium and large.
¿Puedo probármelo? means can I try it on?
lessons.try: Act out a clothing store visit with a partner.

learn: Este (this) and ese (that). Este suéter es bonito. Ese suéter es feo.
Esta and esa are for la words: esta camisa, esa falda.
Me queda bien means it fits me well. Me queda grande means it is too big.
check: It is too big on me
lessons.try: Compare two items of clothing using este and ese.

learn: ¿Cuánto es? asks how much in total. En efectivo means in cash. Con tarjeta means by card.
El cambio is the change you get back.
Count your change carefully and say gracias.
lessons.try: Use play money to buy and pay, counting change in Spanish.

learn: Describe what clothes are made of.
lessons.try: Check labels and say materials.

learn: Esta camisa es más cara que esa.
lessons.try: Compare prices in a catalogue.
Design a shirt and describe it.

check: Para mi abuela means ___ my grandma.
lessons.try: Choose and describe a gift for someone.

check: Es muy pequeña means it's very...
lessons.try: Role-play returning an item.
Store role-play final.

learn: Al lado de (next to), enfrente de (in front of), detrás de (behind), entre (between).
La panadería está al lado del banco. Del is de plus el.
lessons.try: Describe where five buildings are on a town map.

learn: Sigue derecho (go straight). Dobla a la izquierda (turn left). Cruza la calle (cross the street).
La cuadra is the city block. Camina dos cuadras means walk two blocks.
lessons.try: Write directions from your school to a nearby place.

learn: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el museo? Excuse me, where is the museum?
Always thank the person who helps: muchas gracias.
lessons.try: Role-play a tourist asking for directions.

learn: El museo, el estadio, el ayuntamiento.
check: La estación de tren is the...
lessons.try: Label a city map.
Follow Spanish directions on a map.

check: Camina dos cuadras means walk two...
lessons.try: Give directions using blocks and corners.

learn: El metro, el autobús, el taxi.
Tomo el metro: I take the subway.
Mexico City has a big metro.
check: Tomo el metro means I take the...
lessons.try: Plan a trip on a metro map.

learn: Estoy perdido or perdida: I'm lost.
Ask a police officer or shopkeeper.
lessons.try: Role-play being lost and asking for help.
City map treasure hunt.

learn: La olla (pot), la sartén (pan), el horno (oven), el cuchillo (knife), el tazón (bowl).
Ingredientes are ingredients. Una receta is a recipe.
Always cook with an adult and wash your hands first.
lessons.try: Name ten kitchen things in Spanish.

learn: These are command forms, used in recipes.
Mezcla la harina y el agua. Mix the flour and water.
lessons.try: Follow a simple recipe and say each step in Spanish.

learn: Guacamole is made from aguacates, tomate, cebolla (onion), limón and sal.
Corta los aguacates. Añade el tomate. Mezcla todo.
Guacamole comes from Aztec food long ago.
check: The main ingredient of guacamole is...
lessons.try: With an adult, make guacamole and read the steps in Spanish.

learn: Una taza (a cup), una cucharada (a tablespoon).
Una pizca de sal (a pinch of salt).
lessons.try: Read a recipe's measurements aloud.
Follow a recipe with Spanish commands.

learn: Make balls, press and cook on a comal.
check: A comal is a ___ for cooking.
lessons.try: Describe how to make tortillas.

learn: Chocolate caliente is a Mexican tradition.
lessons.try: Draw a molinillo.

learn: Lávate las manos antes de cocinar.
Cuidado con el cuchillo (careful with the knife).
Ask an adult to use the stove.
lessons.try: Make a kitchen safety poster.
Cooking show in Spanish.

learn: Seven countries form Central America, between Mexico and South America.
Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panamá speak Spanish. Belize mostly speaks English.
The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
check: What does the Panama Canal connect?
Which country is in Central America?
lessons.try: Label the Central American countries on a map.

learn: Argentina, Chile, Perú, Colombia, Venezuela, Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay and Uruguay speak Spanish. Brazil speaks Portuguese.
The Andes are the longest mountain range above the sea. The Amazon is a huge river and rainforest.
Machu Picchu is an ancient Inca city high in Peru.
check: Which language does Brazil mainly speak?
lessons.try: Pick a South American country and make a fact card in Spanish.

learn: Inti Raymi in Peru celebrates the sun. Carnaval has parades, music and costumes in many countries.
La Feria de las Flores in Colombia celebrates flowers.
Festivals share music, food and history.
check: La Feria de las Flores is in...
lessons.try: Design a poster for a festival, with three Spanish words.

learn: Connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
check: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and...
lessons.try: Trace a ship's route on a map.

learn: One of the longest rivers in the world.
Flows through Peru, Colombia and Brazil.
check: The Amazon is one of the ___ rivers.
lessons.try: Draw the Amazon and its animals.
Make a fact card about the Galápagos.

learn: The far south of Argentina and Chile.
check: Patagonia is in the far ___ of South America.
lessons.try: Draw a Patagonian landscape.

learn: Led independence movements in South America.
lessons.try: Make a timeline of Bolívar's life.
